subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the equation of the circle whose centre is (−1,2) and which passes through (5,6).

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, SENIOR INTER MATHS-2B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.78 — VSAQ chapter 12 Circle, answer 108.2. It is the right-hand twin of answer 108.1. Printed appearance tag: TS 18. Every number was re-derived and the book is correct: r² = 52 and the circle is x² + y² + 2x − 4y − 47 = 0. insider_note: r² = 52 is not a perfect square, so keep it as 52 all the way — writing r = √52 and squaring it again is where the constant term goes wrong.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find the radius
steps.margin_note: One mark. Work in r² throughout; the square root is never needed.
steps.memory_tip: Radius = distance from centre to the given point. Keep it squared.
lines: Centre C = (−1, 2), point on the circle P = (5, 6)
steps.why: The equation of a circle uses r², so squaring the distance and stopping there avoids an unnecessary surd.
common_mistakes: Taking the square root and then losing accuracy.

steps.label: Write the equation
steps.memory_tip: Centre (−1, 2) gives brackets (x + 1) and (y − 2). Both signs flip.
lines: Circle with centre (−1, 2) and r² = 52 is
steps.why: Expanding the centre-radius form gives the general equation. The constant is 1 + 4 − 52 = −47, which is where the arithmetic mark sits.
